wave.title: shortlink MVP
wave.goal: A working URL shortener (shorten, redirect, per-link click count) built under strict quality gates, to validate autonome's ability to implement within enforced limits.

discussion.text: Out of scope for the wave: auth, custom aliases, expiration, edit/delete, rate limiting. Proposed split: links (POST /links, GET /{code} 302) then click-stats (clicks table, GET /links/{code}/stats).
Asked for more gates (style, linter) since the goal is to validate autonome implementing under limits.
Proposed ruff format, stricter ruff, mypy strict, coverage >= 90%, import-linter contracts; as a separate first feature quality-gates.
Yes: three features, quality-gates -> links -> click-stats.

features.title: Quality gates: strict lint, format, types, coverage, import boundaries

tasks.title: Stricter ruff rules and ruff format

review_findings.issue: The gates don't run `ruff format --check`, and my Bash access was denied, so I couldn't run it myself. I read src/shortlink/app.py, src/shortlink/__init__.py and tests/test_health.py by hand and they look format-clean. This acceptance criterion is checked by reading, not by running the command.

The gate list for this run (ruff, pytest, format) doesn't include mypy, so the 'uv run mypy exits 0' criterion isn't checked automatically. I couldn't run it either because Bash was denied. From reading the code it should pass: app.py health() is already typed `-> dict[str, str]`, test_health is now `-> None`, and FastAPI/TestClient ship type hints. Someone should still confirm mypy is added to the gate config, or run it once by hand.

The dev group lists mypy as `"mypy>=2.4.1"` and switches to a multi-line array, while the other deps are written inline as `>=major` floors. This is harmless and is just how `uv add` formats it. No scope creep: the diff only adds mypy, [tool.mypy] (strict, 3.13, files src+tests) and one test annotation. There's no `# type: ignore` and no per-module overrides.

Nothing runs lint-imports yet. The gates listed are ruff, pytest, format and types, so these contracts are only checked when someone runs them by hand. This change can't fix that, since gate config sits outside the task, but someone needs to add lint-imports to the autonome gate config, or the layer rules won't be enforced for the links/db/stats features.

I couldn't run anything here (Bash was denied), so I haven't seen 'lint-imports: 2 kept' or the temporary `import sqlite3` check fail. The config looks right: grimp adds stdlib modules as external packages when include_external_packages=true, so forbidding sqlite3 should work and no workaround comment is needed. Still, check the implementer's handoff for the output of both checks before merging.

The contract named 'routes over logic over db' has one real layer for now (shortlink.app); stats, links and db don't exist yet. So it currently checks nothing. That's expected for this task, but a typo in a later module name (e.g. shortlink.database) would be skipped silently as an optional layer instead of being reported.

tasks.title: Coverage with pytest-cov
reasons:
review: still blocking after 2 encore(s):
- .coverage: The diff commits the binary `.coverage` data file, a local artifact from a test run, in the same change that adds `.coverage` to .gitignore. .gitignore does not untrack a file that is already committed, so every later `pytest --cov` run rewrites

review_findings.issue: [tool.pytest.ini_options] has no `addopts = "--cov"`, so a plain `uv run pytest` won't measure or enforce coverage. The 90% check only runs when the gate is called with `--cov=shortlink --cov-fail-under=90`. The task defines exactly that command, so this isn't a defect. Just make sure the metronome's pytest gate calls it with those flags, or the fail_under = 90 in [tool.coverage.report] never takes effect.

Couldn't run the gate command myself because Bash was denied. From reading the code, the only module (app.py, /health) is fully hit by tests/test_health.py, so coverage should be 100% and well above 90%. Config matches the task: source = ["shortlink"], branch = true, show_missing, fail_under = 90, pytest-cov in the dev group. The lockfile and .gitignore changes are in scope.

features.title: Links: shorten a URL and redirect

tasks.title: SQLite connection, schema and test fixture
reasons: SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'I', "Internal S"... is not valid JSON
metronome: imports: the same failure repeated

review_findings.issue: test_lifespan_creates_schema reads the DB via db.connect() and relies on the client fixture's monkeypatched SHORTLINK_DB still being set. That works, but the dependency is implicit. Note for later: no test goes through the `Conn` dependency in an actual request yet. That's fine here since no route uses it until the links task.

post_link catches only InvalidURLError. The RuntimeError that create_link raises after 5 collisions comes back as a bare 500, not the JSON {"detail": ...} the project rules ask for. The task didn't ask to map it, so it isn't blocking, but a 503 with a detail would fit the convention better.

validate_url only rejects characters where str.isspace() is true. Control characters that aren't whitespace (e.g. \x00, \x7f) are accepted and stored. The task doesn't require rejecting them, but GET /{code} will later put this value in a Location header.

create_link catches every sqlite3.IntegrityError and treats it as a code collision. A different constraint failure (e.g. NOT NULL) would use up all 5 attempts and then show up as the misleading 'no free code' RuntimeError. It can't happen with today's inputs, so this is just a note.

test_health_not_shadowed passes whatever order the routes are registered in: 'health' is in RESERVED, so a shadowing /{code} would still 404 rather than return {"status": "ok"}... actually, it would return 404 and the test would fail, so the test does guard against shadowing. The only gap is that no test pins a reserved word that has no route (e.g. GET /docs or GET /links) to the 404 fall-through. That is fine for this task.

The redirect target comes straight from the DB with no re-check. That's safe today because POST /links only stores validated http(s) URLs. If any other write path is added later, it needs the same validation, or this becomes an open redirect to a javascript: or other scheme.

features.title: Click stats: count redirects per link

review_findings.issue: record_click annotates conn as sqlite3.Connection rather than reusing the db module's types; harmless since the route passes the injected Conn, but keep the layer consistent when get_stats is added.

test_new_link_has_zero_clicks only checks that created_at is a non-empty string. It doesn't compare it with the links row, so a get_stats that returned the wrong column there (for example url) would still fail the test, but a wrong timestamp source wouldn't. Comparing against the DB value would close that gap. It's a note, not a blocker.

friction: The first attempt to write stats.py through a Bash heredoc was denied because the session ran in don't-ask mode. The agent switched to Read and Edit, which worked, and lost one step. The write-file rules are not documented for agents.
The agent did not read any briefing, despite the user's explicit instruction.
The agent's claim that the tests cover both get_stats paths was not checked against a coverage run. The coverage gate passed only afterwards, from the metronome.
The agent tried a Bash heredoc to rewrite source files and was denied by the permission mode. It should have used Edit from the start.
The formatter failed on the first gate run because the agent split the SQL string over two lines. The project formatter's line-joining preference is not written down anywhere the agent could see.
The final message says the briefing suggested comparing a sorted list in the table test. The transcript never shows the briefing being read, so I could not check that claim.
The Bash heredoc write was denied in don't-ask mode, which cost one wasted call before the agent switched to Edit.
The agent told the user that full Bash was blocked, but `autonome-gates --fast` ran fine. Only the write-style command was denied, so the claim overstates the limit.
The agent did not run the imports and coverage gates and left them to the metronome. They passed, but it had no early signal on them.
The briefing the user mentioned was never located, so the agent's claim that nothing was ambiguous has no written source to check against.
The first Bash call (cat of several files plus pyproject) was denied because the session is in don't-ask mode. The agent switched to Glob and Read, which cost one round trip.

The agent was told to 'read the briefing' but never opened one. It went straight to reading the code and implemented from the task title and its own assumptions, so there's a risk it missed requirements.

The agent's mypy failure came from a test reaching a module attribute (`secrets`) that `links` doesn't explicitly export. Test conventions for monkeypatching stdlib modules aren't written down, and the agent only found the problem by running the gates.
The briefing the task said to read does not appear in the transcript. The first visible action is a cat of app.py, tests and .gitignore, so it is unclear how the requirements were taken in.

The agent ran the fast gates before it had fixed everything, and the types gate caught a bug in the freshly written test. It should have used the generator and its connection correctly the first time.
A chained sed and ruff Bash command was denied by the permission mode. This cost a round trip, and the agent switched to Edit.
No metronome gate runs were recorded for this session. The gate results come only from the agent's own autonome-gates commands in the transcript.

The import-linter contract and the plan conflict: the rehearsal notes assumed only direct imports count, but the contract also blocks indirect ones. The agent found this only after writing all the code and running the gates.
The agent searched the autonome project memory and tried decision_propose, but the tool was denied in don't-ask mode, so there was no way to register the blocker in the process.
The stop hook (metronome) asked to fix the cause three times while the cause was a gate rule the agent may not change, which meant a stalemate that needs a human or a plan change.
The first run showed 'autonome-context is unreachable' and uv built a fresh venv on CPython 3.14.5 although the project targets 3.13; the agent did not remark on this.

The first Bash call was a long compound command (grep; pytest | tail; echo; git status; cat .gitignore). It was denied because the session ran in don't-ask mode. The agent re-ran only the pytest part and used Read for the other files, which cost one extra round trip.
The agent hit the .gitignore gap only after running coverage and checking the files, not up front.
The agent ran `autonome-gates --fast`, which skips the imports gate. It then told the user it hadn't run imports, so the process leaves a gap the agent had to point out.

Two Bash calls were denied because the session ran in don't-ask mode: the cp backup of app.py and a lint-imports call using `${pipestatus[1]}`. The agent switched to Read/Edit and then re-ran without the exit-status part.

The agent could not back up app.py, so it reverted by hand with Edit. Its claim that app.py ended up identical to the original is supported by git status, which shows only pyproject.toml and uv.lock modified.
The first `lint-imports` output showed 'Analyzed 3 files, 1 dependencies', so only a small part of the code was exercised before the negative test.
Don't-ask mode blocked Bash for `git rm --cached` and `rm`. Because of that, the agent could not fix the reviewer's blocking issue in two review rounds.

Running `uv run pytest --cov` created and staged `.coverage` before .gitignore had an entry for it. There is no convention that a coverage task updates .gitignore first, and the gates do not catch a tracked data file.
Two review rounds raised the same issue. The second round was spent on a step the agent already knew it could not do, and the runner did not unstage the file between the rounds.
The `.gitignore` edit alone does nothing for a file that is already tracked. The agent said so, but the first fix attempt was only half of what the reviewer asked for.
The agent's first summary said the task was done without saying `.coverage` was staged.
A chained Bash command (grep, mypy, grep and autonome-gates) was denied in don't-ask mode. The agent had to split it into separate calls (Bash, Grep, Grep), which cost a few turns.
The 'Read the briefing' step left no visible trace in the transcript. The agent started by dumping pyproject, source and tests with cat, so it is unclear what the briefing required.
The `pyproject.toml` dev list was rewritten from one line to a multi-line list, a small formatting change that has nothing to do with mypy.
The task said to read the briefing first, but the transcript shows no briefing read. Briefing contents are quoted from memory or from context the scribe cannot see, so the scope cannot be audited.
uv created the venv with CPython 3.14.5, while CLAUDE.md says Python 3.13. `requires-python >=3.13` allows it, but the gates ran on a different interpreter than documented.

The final command chained `autonome-gates --fast; git status --short`, and the output was truncated. The diff the agent produced is not shown, and this record relied on its own summary for the file changes.

tune:
Propus 6 convenções, todas ainda como "proposed". Não fiz plan_draft: nenhum gate novo era preciso, porque types, imports e coverage já existem. O projeto não tinha convenções, então não afrouxei nenhuma.

- **#93, escrever arquivos com Edit/Write, sem Bash:** heredoc, cp e comandos encadeados foram negados em 8 dos 11 handoffs (34, 41, 63, 70, 76, 80, 84, 89).
- **#94, ler o briefing primeiro e citar no final:** a leitura não deixou rastro em 7 handoffs (30, 34, 37, 70, 76, 80, 89).
- **#95, rodar lint-imports e coverage antes de terminar:** o `--fast` pula esses dois gates. O imports falhou em 2 de 8 execuções e o agente só descobriu tarde (63, 66, 80, 89).
- **#96, pôr arquivos gerados no .gitignore antes de gerá-los:** o `.coverage` foi staged e queimou 2 rodadas de review (37, 63, task 23).
- **#97, todo erro de domínio vira JSON `{"detail"}`:** o RuntimeError do `create_link` virou 500 puro (reviews das tasks 26 e 27).
- **#98, fixar Python 3.13 no `.python-version`:** o uv criou o venv em 3.14.5, contra o 3.13 do CLAUDE.md (30, 66).

Nenhuma task de correção veio de soundcheck, porque o soundcheck está desligado na configuração de gates. Nenhuma task ficou bloqueada.
